title: Job contract v1 (frozen): describes work, never a worker
description: The Trillian bridge's job contract. It names an objective, a writable file scope, and one deterministic acceptance command. It deliberately says nothing about which model, arm, tier, or vendor performs the work: that choice belongs to the router (scripts/route.py) and can change from run to run, or from one model generation to the next, without invalidating any contract already written against this schema.

schema.description: Pins the contract to this frozen shape so downstream tooling never has to sniff the version.

id.description: Optional slug used to reference this job from another job's depends_on.

objective.description: What outcome is wanted, in plain language. Never a model instruction or persona.

not.description: Rejects absolute paths (POSIX or drive-letter), parent-directory escapes, and anything under .git — the writable scope must stay a relative subset of the working tree.

files.description: Repo-relative writable scope. Every entry must be relative, contain no '..', and not reach into .git.

not.description: The acceptance field is one shell command, not a script; a newline means two commands got smuggled into one field.

acceptance.description: One shell command. Exit 0 means the objective is done; any other exit code means it is not.

max_files_changed.description: Optional cap on how many files a single attempt may touch.

max_rounds.description: Optional cap on repair/escalation rounds before a lineage is declared failed.

limits.description: Optional numeric guardrails. Both keys are optional; an empty object is valid.

depends_on.description: Optional list of other job ids that must complete before this one is dispatched.

not.description: HARD RULE: the contract never names a model, arm, tier, or vendor/provider. The contract describes the work; a router (not the operator, not the chat model that drafted this JSON) decides who performs it. Baking a model choice into the contract would tie a piece of work to whichever model happened to be current the day the contract was written, and break the moment that model is deprecated, re-priced, or simply beaten by something cheaper. A contract that survives model churn cannot mention one.
